key_insight: Quantum algorithms estimate finite-horizon LQR costs and selected-time controls with polylogarithmic scaling in system size and duration under bounded-parameter and oracle-access assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce computational costs for large-scale linear control problems without constructing a full Riccati solution operator.
method: Reformulate state–costate optimality equations as a multiple-shooting linear system with initial and final conditions.
Prove a horizon-independent condition-number bound under stabilizability and detectability assumptions.
Use quantum linear-system routines to obtain classical estimates of optimal cost and control inputs at a selected time.
evidence_signal: Uniform bounds are established for damped mass–spring chains with two endpoint controls, and numerical experiments support the analysis.
watch_item: Efficiency requires sparse-matrix block-encodings, initial-state preparation, bounded problem parameters, and a fixed number of controls; error dependence is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors.
paper_title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
